title_en: Jiangsu Ruida Ocean Food Co., Ltd. v. People's Government of Dafeng District, Yancheng City, et al. — dispute over administrative licensing of sea area use rights
ruling_gist_en: The holder of the right to use sea areas has the right to apply for renewal before the expiration of the sea area use term. However, if the government and the holder have agreed through an administrative agreement that the right will not be renewed after expiration, such agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws and regulations and shall be deemed valid.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd. v. Yancheng Dafeng District People's Government, et al. — Dispute over Administrative Licensing of Sea Area Use Rights

[Ruling Summary]

A holder of a sea area use right has the right to apply for an extension before the expiration of the use period. However, if the government and the holder agree in an administrative agreement that the right will not be renewed upon expiration, such an agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of Chinese laws and regulations and shall be deemed valid.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., domiciled at North Weisi Road, Marine Economic Comprehensive Development Zone, Dafeng District, Yancheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Hong, Executive Director of the company.

Defendant: Yancheng Dafeng District People's Government, domiciled at No. 1 Dadonghua Road, Dafeng District, Yancheng City.

Legal Representative: Song Yong, District Mayor.

Defendant: Yancheng Dafeng District Natural Resources and Planning Bureau, domiciled at Xingfu West Street, Dafeng District, Yancheng City.

Legal Representative: Shang Mingxing, Director of the Bureau.

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court against the defendants, Yancheng Dafeng District People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Dafeng District Government) and Yancheng Dafeng District Natural Resources and Planning Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau), concerning a dispute over administrative licensing of sea area use rights.

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., alleged: In August 2015, the plaintiff, through a bidding process, signed a contract with the defendant Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau for the transfer of the right to use sea areas for laver cultivation in Dongsha, with a term of three years. In early 2018, the plaintiff applied to the defendant Dafeng District Government for an extension of the sea area use right. In May of the same year, the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau issued a "Reply on the Denial of Extension of Sea Area Use Right," stating that the plaintiff's report on the application for extension of the sea area use right had been received, and the reply stated that the sea area use right contract explicitly stipulated that the right would not be renewed upon expiration. Subsequently, the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau issued a "Notice on Clearing Laver Cultivation in Dongsha" to the plaintiff, requiring the owners whose sea area use rights had expired to immediately stop laver cultivation activities and dismantle all artificial facilities and equipment. The plaintiff argued that since its application for extension was submitted to the original approving authority, the Dafeng District Government, it should have been responded to by the Dafeng District Government. The Dafeng District Government did not make a decision on whether to grant the extension before the expiration of the original administrative license, and therefore, it should be deemed that the extension was granted. According to Article 26 of the Sea Area Use Management Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Sea Area Use Management Law), the holder of a sea area use right has the right to apply for an extension before the expiration of the term. Except when the sea area use right needs to be withdrawn due to public interest or national security, the original approving people's government shall approve the extension. In summary, the plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Revoke the "Reply on the Denial of Extension of Sea Area Use Right" issued by the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau to the plaintiff; 2. Order the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau and the Dafeng District Government to perform their statutory duties and legally extend the plaintiff's sea area use right.

The defendants, Dafeng District Government and Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau, argued: The sea area use right transfer contract and the sea area use right certificate both explicitly stated that the right would not be renewed upon expiration. The application for extension should not apply to sea area use rights obtained through bidding. Part of the sea area for laver cultivation in Dongsha overlaps with or is adjacent to the Yancheng Wetland Rare Birds National Nature Reserve. Cultivating laver in this sea area violates relevant regulations on nature reserve management. Moreover, cultivation in the experimental zone of the reserve must also be approved by the reserve management authority. The Dafeng District government departments had applied to the reserve management authority but did not obtain approval. Part of the Dongsha cultivation sea area falls within the ecological red line. According to the ecological red line protection plan, a system of restricted approvals is implemented for the red line area, strictly controlling development intensity and strengthening ecological protection and restoration. During 2018, the work on the application of Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland for World Natural Heritage was ongoing. The Dongsha cultivation sea area overlaps with or is adjacent to the nominated site for the Yellow Sea Wetland World Heritage application. Continued laver cultivation in this sea area is detrimental to the protection of the heritage site. Currently, the central government is adopting stricter supervision measures for the oceans, and during the supervision process, it specifically pointed out problems existing in the cultivation in the Dafeng Dongsha sea area. The Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland, as a habitat for red-crowned cranes and other migratory birds and a nominated World Heritage site, requires the restoration of marine ecology by returning aquaculture areas to wetlands in its vicinity. This is the current trend and is necessary for the protection of the long-term public interest. In summary, the defendants requested the court to reject the plaintiff's claims.

The Shanghai Maritime Court found at first instance:

In August 2015, the plaintiff, Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., participated in a bidding process organized by the defendant Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau for the transfer of sea area use rights. Through bidding, the plaintiff signed three contracts for the first round of transfer of sea area use rights for laver cultivation in Dongsha in 2015. These contracts corresponded to the third, fourth, and fifth bid sections respectively. The transferred sea areas were all located in the Dongsha Radial Sand Ridges, and the designated use of the sea areas was laver cultivation. The sea area areas specified in the contracts were 145.099 hectares, 97.668 hectares, and 142.991 hectares respectively. The sea area use rights periods stipulated in the above contracts were all from August 20, 2015, to June 30, 2018. Article 10 of each of the above contracts stated: "Upon the expiration of the contract, the sea area use right shall terminate, and this sea area use right shall not be renewed." Subsequently, the plaintiff obtained three corresponding sea area use right certificates. The registration authority indicated on the certificates was the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau, and the issuing authority was the defendant Dafeng District Government. The certificates stated the termination date as June 30, 2018, and noted that "the sea area obtained through bidding shall not be renewed after expiration."

On March 29, 2018, the plaintiff, Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., mailed an application for extension of the sea area use right to the defendant Dafeng District Government and the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau. The Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau issued a "Reply on the Denial of Extension of Sea Area Use Right" to the plaintiff, stating that the plaintiff's report on the application for extension of the sea area use right had been received. The reply stated that the sea area use right contract explicitly stipulated that the right would not be renewed upon expiration. Moreover, according to the "Notice on Further Strengthening the Management of Aquaculture Sea Use in Dongsha" issued by the Dafeng District Government in May 2014, after the expiration of the sea area use right, the original sea user shall promptly and unconditionally return the beach, and the competent authority shall organize a bidding process for the transfer. Therefore, the corresponding sea area certificate had already noted "no renewal after expiration." The plaintiff received the above reply on May 26, 2018. On August 30, 2018, the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau issued a "Notice on Clearing Laver Cultivation in Dongsha" to all laver cultivation owners, stating that according to Article 29 of the Sea Area Use Management Law, if the sea area use right expires and an extension is not applied for or the application for extension is not approved, the sea area use right shall terminate. After the termination of the sea area use right, the original holder shall remove all sea use facilities and structures that may cause marine environmental pollution or affect other sea use projects. According to legal provisions and requirements from higher authorities, owners in the Dongsha sea area whose use rights have expired shall immediately stop laver cultivation activities, dismantle all artificial facilities and equipment, and clear marine floating garbage and production and domestic waste.

It was further found that the sea area for which the plaintiff originally obtained the use right was located on the Dongsha Radial Sand Ridges in Dafeng District, adjacent to the Jiangsu Province Marine Ecological Red Line Zone, and close to the Yancheng Wetland Rare Birds National Nature Reserve and the Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland. Before the plaintiff obtained the sea area use right in question, the relevant sea area had also been transferred through bidding in 2012. After the expiration of the sea area use right in 2015, the local government organized a new bidding process, and the plaintiff won the bid and obtained the sea area use right in question. In January 2018, the Yancheng Municipal Government officially submitted the formal World Heritage application text to the World Heritage Centre. On August 24, 2018, the General Office of the Yancheng Municipal People's Government issued a "Notice from the General Office of the Municipal Government on Doing a Good Job in the National Inspection and Evaluation of Heritage Nomination Sites." The attached key task assignment sheet stated that the defendant Dafeng District Government was required to clear laver cultivation in Dongsha. In July 2019, the Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland was successfully inscribed on the World Natural Heritage list following a vote at the World Natural Heritage Convention.

The Shanghai Maritime Court held at first instance:

Pursuant to Articles 7 and 17 of the Sea Area Use Management Law, the defendant Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau, as the marine administrative authority, has the statutory duty to manage the sea areas in question and the power to review applications for sea area use. The reply it issued in this case falls within its administrative authority and does not exceed its powers. The defendant Dafeng District Government, as the original approving government authority for sea area use, has the statutory duty to decide whether to approve applications for sea area use.

The main issues in dispute in this case are whether the refusal by the defendants Dafeng District Government and Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau to extend the plaintiff's sea area use right has a factual and legal basis, and whether the "Reply on the Denial of Extension of Sea Area Use Right" issued by the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau to the plaintiff is valid. First, according to Article 20 of the Sea Area Use Management Law, sea area use rights may be obtained through bidding or auction. The bidding or auction plan is formulated by the marine administrative authority and implemented after being submitted to the people's government with approval authority for approval. The terms of the sea area use right transfer contract are a major component of the bidding plan, and formulating these contract terms falls within the authority of the Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau and the Dafeng District Government. Second, Article 10 of the sea area use right transfer contract in question explicitly states: "Upon the expiration of the contract, the sea area use right shall terminate, and this sea area use right shall not be renewed." The meaning is clear and unambiguous. There was no fraud or duress in the signing of the relevant contract. The plaintiff should have known and understood the meaning of the relevant contract terms. By participating in the bidding and signing the contract, the plaintiff accepted the bidding plan and the restrictive conditions of the contract terms. The agreement in the sea area use right transfer contract that "no renewal upon expiration" is a valid agreement. Finally, the plaintiff's main argument that this clause is invalid is that it violates the relevant provisions of Article 26 of the Sea Area Use Management Law concerning the right of the sea area use right holder to apply for an extension. The court holds that this article is a general provision regarding the right of the sea area use right holder to apply for an extension and is not a mandatory provision. It does not preclude the government authority and the sea area use right holder from changing, through an explicit agreement, whether and how to renew the right after expiration. Given that sea area use right, as a state-owned natural resource, is scarce, the government authority's use of periodic bidding to transfer sea area use rights is a means of promoting the optimal allocation of natural resources through market mechanisms. It maximizes and safeguards the value of state assets through competitive methods and reflects a more transparent and open exercise of the government's authority in managing the transfer of sea area use rights. Particularly considering that the sea area in question is adjacent to a national nature reserve, the Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland, and the Jiangsu Province Marine Ecological Red Line, there is a degree of uncertainty as to whether continuous cultivation and development can be sustained. The government's use of this clause to place certain restrictions on the transfer of use rights for the relevant sea area is reasonable and does not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations. In summary, both the sea area use right transfer contract and the sea area use right certificate explicitly state "no renewal upon expiration." After the sea area use right expired, the two defendants had the authority, based on relevant laws and regulations and taking into account the actual situation of sea area management and development, to decide whether to continue transferring the sea area and the specific method of transfer.

During the trial, the defendants Dafeng District Government and Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau stated that China's offshore sea areas are facing problems of overdevelopment and severe damage to the marine ecology. Therefore, the state has placed unprecedented importance on the protection of the marine ecological environment, organizing multiple marine inspections and specifically pointing out problems in the cultivation in the Dafeng Dongsha sea area. The Yancheng Yellow Sea Wetland, as a habitat for red-crowned cranes and other migratory birds and a nominated World Heritage site, requires the restoration of marine ecology by returning aquaculture areas to wet lands in its vicinity. This is the current trend and is necessary for the protection of the long-term public interest. Considering these factors comprehensively, the government decided not to organize the transfer of the sea area in question for the time being. The court holds that the two defendants' decision not to immediately transfer the use rights for the relevant sea area, on the grounds of safeguarding the public interest, falls within the scope of their administrative powers to exercise sea area management authority and is not improper. The Dafeng District Natural Resources Bureau, as the marine administrative authority and a subordinate agency of the Dafeng District Government, its reply denying the extension to the plaintiff is a lawful and valid reply.

Pursuant to Article 7, paragraph 1, Article 17, paragraph 1, Article 20, and Article 26 of the Sea Area Use Management Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 69 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai Maritime Court rendered the following judgment on December 4, 2019:

The claims of the plaintiff, Jiangsu Ruida Marine Food Co., Ltd., against the defendants, Yancheng Dafeng District People's Government and Yancheng Dafeng District Natural Resources and Planning Bureau, are dismissed.

After the judgment was pronounced at first instance, none of the parties appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
